name: Lies, Lies, Lies

items.name: Paperclip money clip (Prada)
items.fact: In 2017 Prada sold a sterling-silver money clip shaped exactly like an ordinary office paperclip. In the USA it cost about $185, and people online could not stop laughing.

items.name: Aeroplane handbag (Louis Vuitton)
items.fact: Louis Vuitton sold a handbag shaped like a small aeroplane, covered in its famous monogram, for about $39,000. Many people pointed out that some real second-hand planes cost less.

items.name: Branded brick (Supreme)
items.fact: The streetwear brand Supreme once sold an ordinary red clay brick with its logo stamped on it, for $30. It sold out at once, and resellers then asked up to $1,000 for one.

items.name: Pigeon clutch bag (JW Anderson)
items.fact: The London designer JW Anderson sold a clutch bag in the shape of a grey city pigeon. Carried under your arm, it looks as if you have just picked up a real bird from the street.

items.name: French-fries phone case (Moschino)
items.fact: For his first Moschino show in 2014, the designer Jeremy Scott sent out a phone case shaped like a red carton of French fries. The whole collection copied the look of fast-food packaging.

items.name: A bag smaller than a grain of salt (MSCHF)
items.fact: The New York art group MSCHF made a tiny green handbag in the style of Louis Vuitton, smaller than a grain of sea salt. You need a microscope to see it. It sold at auction for $63,750.

items.name: A bag made of 99% air (Coperni)
items.fact: The Paris label Coperni made a handbag from silica aerogel, a material that NASA has used in space and that is about 99% air. It looks like frozen smoke and weighs almost nothing.

items.name: Delivery-company T-shirt (Vetements)
items.fact: The Paris label Vetements sold a yellow T-shirt with the red logo of the delivery company DHL on it, for around £185. It looks almost the same as the T-shirts DHL drivers wear to work.

items.name: Pre-dirtied trainers (Golden Goose)
items.fact: The Italian brand Golden Goose sells expensive trainers that leave the factory already scuffed, scratched and dirty-looking, so that brand-new shoes look as if their owner has worn them for years.

items.name: The first Birkin bag (Hermès)
items.fact: The very first Hermès Birkin bag, made for the singer and actress Jane Birkin and carried by her for years, sold at auction in Paris in 2025 for €8.6 million, a record for a handbag.

fakes.name: Perfumed umbrella
fakes.fact: A French fashion house sells a black umbrella whose fabric is treated with its best-known perfume, so it smells of the scent every time it rains. It costs €890 and the smell lasts about a year.

fakes.name: Marble sticky notes
fakes.fact: An Italian design brand sells a block of “sticky notes” cut from thin white marble. You write on them with a special pencil, and the block weighs nearly two kilos.

fakes.name: Cashmere oven gloves
fakes.fact: A London fashion house sells oven gloves knitted from pure cashmere in its classic colours, for £420 a pair. The label warns that they must never touch anything hot.

fakes.name: Leather ice scraper
fakes.fact: A German luxury brand sells a scraper for clearing ice off car windscreens, covered in hand-stitched calf leather with its logo in gold. It costs €340 and comes with its own dust bag.

fakes.name: Holiday sand in a jar
fakes.fact: A Milan label sells small glass jars of sand from the beach below its founder's summer house in Sardinia, as a “souvenir of summer”. Each jar costs €95, and there is a waiting list.

fakes.name: Gold receipts
fakes.fact: A Paris jewellery brand prints its receipts on thin gold-coloured metal instead of paper. Customers keep them as souvenirs, and some sell them online for more than €50 each.

fakes.name: Porcelain bubble wrap
fakes.fact: A Milan design house sells a sheet of “bubble wrap” made of thin white porcelain, for €480. Each bubble is shaped by hand, and the label warns that none of them can be popped.

fakes.name: Silver shoelaces
fakes.fact: A Paris fashion house sells one pair of plain white shoelaces in a leather box for €220. Each lace has a thin thread of real silver woven into it, so it slowly turns grey.

fakes.name: Lambskin washing-up gloves
fakes.fact: A Milan fashion house sells yellow washing-up gloves made of soft lambskin, with its logo on each wrist, for €480 a pair. They are not waterproof.

fakes.name: Diamond bicycle bell
fakes.fact: A London jeweller sells a bicycle bell set with small diamonds, for £3,800. It is made for folding bikes, and the jeweller says it rings exactly in the key of C.

fake: Give it a real-sounding name, maybe with a brand name in brackets.
Something ordinary that a luxury brand turned into something expensive.
A fashion house, a jeweller or a designer, and a real city.
The material, the craft or the idea behind it.
A price, and who buys it.
A date, a waiting list or a small problem it still has.
tips: Be specific: numbers, dates and real places make a lie believable.
Give it a small problem (“it isn't waterproof”): perfect things sound fake.
Make both talks the same length and give them the same confidence.
Don't laugh. Decide now who says which one.
